moods.name: Tender
moods.description: soft edges, warm light, quiet attention

directors.name: Sofia Coppola
directors.styleDescription: Dreamy, slow, intimate. She films loneliness as something beautiful. Distance between people, silence, golden-hour light.
shootingPrompts: Film yourself from far away — don't zoom in
Look for light that makes ordinary things look like memories
Capture a moment of waiting or stillness
Let silence be part of the scene
directors.brief: Look for the light that makes ordinary things feel like memories. Stay far away. Let silence be part of the frame.
directors.question1: Did you find a moment today that already felt like a memory?
directors.question2: What was the quietest part of your day, and what was happening in it?

directors.name: Wong Kar-wai
directors.styleDescription: Blurred motion, saturated color, longing. He films time passing and emotion that goes unexpressed.
shootingPrompts: Use slow motion on something mundane
Film reflections — mirrors, windows, puddles
Find a color in your day and let it dominate the frame
Capture someone from behind or at a distance
directors.brief: Find one color that belongs to today, and let it follow you. Watch the world slow down, even when it shouldn't.
directors.question1: Was there something today you felt but didn't say out loud?
directors.question2: If today had a color, what was it, and why?

directors.name: Hirokazu Kore-eda
directors.styleDescription: Quiet observation of everyday family life. He finds meaning in routine gestures and unspoken love.
shootingPrompts: Film a meal, or someone preparing food
Capture a habit — something you do without thinking
Look for small acts of care between people
Film someone doing something ordinary, from a respectful distance
directors.brief: Notice the small acts of care between people — yours, theirs. The meaning is in what is done, not in what is said.
directors.question1: Did someone care for you today, even in a small way?
directors.question2: What ordinary thing did you do today that someone, somewhere, would have called love?

directors.name: Céline Sciamma
directors.styleDescription: Precise, tender, and politically aware. She films looking — who watches, who is seen, what that means.
shootingPrompts: Film yourself or someone looking at something
Notice a moment of being seen or unseen
Find a small detail that tells a whole story
Capture eye contact, or the absence of it
directors.brief: Pay attention to who you looked at today, and who looked at you. Let one small detail tell the whole story.
directors.question1: Did you feel truly seen by someone today?
directors.question2: Who or what caught your eye today, and what did you not say about it?

directors.name: Darren Aronofsky
directors.styleDescription: Visceral, claustrophobic, obsessive. He puts the camera close — inside the experience, not watching it.
shootingPrompts: Film extreme close-ups of hands, eyes, objects
Use handheld — let the camera breathe with you
Capture repetition — something done over and over
Film from an uncomfortable angle
directors.brief: Get close. Notice what your hands kept doing today, what you kept returning to. Let the camera breathe with you.
directors.question1: Did you keep doing something today without quite knowing why?
directors.question2: What were you doing when you weren't doing anything?

directors.name: Lynne Ramsay
directors.styleDescription: Fragmented, poetic, trauma-adjacent. She films the interior world through exterior details — what objects carry.
shootingPrompts: Find an object that holds a feeling today
Film texture — surfaces, fabric, skin, walls
Capture something broken, worn, or imperfect
Let the frame be incomplete — cut off heads, cut off hands
directors.brief: Find an object today that holds a feeling you haven't named. Let the frame stay incomplete.
directors.question1: Did something small carry more weight today than it should have?
directors.question2: What stayed with you longer than it should have today, and where did it come from?

directors.name: Xavier Dolan
directors.styleDescription: Emotional, dramatic, personal. He films big feelings in confined spaces — confrontation, longing, identity.
shootingPrompts: Film a conversation — even if it's one-sided
Use slow motion on an emotional moment
Let music play while you film — feel the contrast
Film yourself or someone mid-feeling, not explaining it
directors.brief: Don't explain the feeling. Let it be loud, even if no one else can see it. Film the moment, not the reason.
directors.question1: Did you feel something today that was bigger than the moment that caused it?
directors.question2: What did you almost say today, and to whom?

directors.name: Park Chan-wook
directors.styleDescription: Precise, unsettling, visually controlled. He films tension through symmetry and unexpected stillness.
shootingPrompts: Look for symmetry in your environment
Film something that feels slightly wrong or off
Use a very still shot of something that should be moving
Find beauty in an uncomfortable place
directors.brief: Find something that feels slightly off today. Stay in the discomfort. Look at it longer than feels right.
directors.question1: Did something feel a little wrong today, even if you couldn't say why?
directors.question2: What did you choose not to look at today?

directors.name: Agnès Varda
directors.styleDescription: Curious, warm, playful. She films the world like she just discovered it — especially what others walk past.
shootingPrompts: Film something small that no one else noticed today
Follow your curiosity — film whatever pulls your eye
Capture a stranger's world without disturbing it
Find something that makes you want to ask a question
directors.brief: Follow your curiosity. Stop where it pulls you. Film what others walked past without noticing.
directors.question1: Did you go somewhere today just because you were curious?
directors.question2: What surprised you today, even briefly?

directors.name: Richard Linklater
directors.styleDescription: Conversational, real-time, unhurried. He films time passing through people talking and being together.
shootingPrompts: Film a real conversation, or record yourself talking to camera
Capture a transition — leaving somewhere, arriving somewhere
Film the in-between moments of your day
Let the camera roll longer than feels comfortable
directors.brief: Stay in the in-between today. Don't rush from one thing to the next. Film a transition, not a destination.
directors.question1: Did you let yourself linger today, even briefly?
directors.question2: What was the longest conversation you had with yourself today?

directors.name: Wim Wenders
directors.styleDescription: Road-like, melancholic, wide-open. He films landscapes and solitude as characters.
shootingPrompts: Film a long shot of wherever you are — don't move the camera
Capture the horizon or a wide empty space
Film yourself or someone moving through space from far away
Look for signs, roads, windows — in-between spaces
directors.brief: Find a wide, open space today and let it sit. Don't fill the frame. Let the horizon do the talking.
directors.question1: Did you spend time alone today on purpose?
directors.question2: Where did your mind go when nothing was asking for it?

directors.name: Jim Jarmusch
directors.styleDescription: Deadpan, slow, coolly observational. He finds dry humor and poetry in ordinary moments and waiting.
shootingPrompts: Film a moment of waiting — don't cut away
Capture something mundane as if it's fascinating
Look for irony or absurdity in an everyday scene
Film with complete stillness — no movement, no explanation
directors.brief: Find a moment of waiting today and stay in it. Let the boring part be interesting. Don't cut away.
directors.question1: Was there a moment of waiting today that was secretly better than the thing you were waiting for?
directors.question2: What's something ordinary that you saw today and quietly liked?

directors.name: Christopher Nolan
directors.styleDescription: Epic, precise, time-obsessed. He films urgency and scale — even small scenes feel like they matter enormously.
shootingPrompts: Film something with a sense of countdown or deadline
Capture architecture or scale — make it feel monumental
Use cuts that feel urgent — don't linger
Film a decision point — a door, a choice, a moment before
directors.brief: Treat today like it matters. Find the scale in small things. Capture the moment before a decision.
directors.question1: Did you make a decision today that quietly mattered?
directors.question2: What were you choosing today, even if no one else could see the choice?

directors.name: David Fincher
directors.styleDescription: Cold, precise, controlled. He films systems and detail — everything is deliberate, nothing is accidental.
shootingPrompts: Film with extreme stillness — no shaking, no accident
Find a scene with artificial light — lamps, screens, neon
Capture order or disorder — things arranged or falling apart
Film a process — something being done step by step
directors.brief: Notice what's deliberate in your day. Watch what's arranged, and what's falling apart. Stay still.
directors.question1: Did something today go exactly the way you planned?
directors.question2: What detail did you notice today that no one else would have?

directors.name: Denis Villeneuve
directors.styleDescription: Slow-burn intensity, vast scale, silence as weight. He films awe and dread in equal measure.
shootingPrompts: Film something vast — sky, a building, a crowd from far
Use a very long pause before or after something happens
Capture a moment of confrontation or first contact
Find the silence in your environment and hold it
directors.brief: Find the silence today and hold it. Let something be vast. Wait longer than feels comfortable.
directors.question1: Did you feel small today, in a good way?
directors.question2: What were you sitting with today that didn't have a name?

directors.name: Paul Thomas Anderson
directors.styleDescription: Operatic, character-obsessed, long takes. He films people with intensity — like they're about to break or explode.
shootingPrompts: Film someone's face for longer than feels normal
Capture a power dynamic — who leads, who follows
Use a slow tracking shot — follow someone walking
Film an environment that reveals character — a desk, a room
directors.brief: Look at someone today longer than feels normal — yourself in a mirror, or a stranger across the room.
directors.question1: Did you notice someone today who was holding something in?
directors.question2: Who had power in your day today, and how could you tell?

directors.name: Wes Anderson
directors.styleDescription: Symmetrical, pastel, deadpan. He films life as a precisely designed world where everything is placed on purpose.
shootingPrompts: Find perfect symmetry and film straight-on
Look for pastel colors or strong flat color blocks
Film a collection of objects arranged deliberately
Use a slow pan left or right — perfectly level
directors.brief: Find perfect symmetry today and film it straight on. Treat ordinary things like they were placed on purpose.
directors.question1: Did you arrange anything today, even just a small thing on a desk?
directors.question2: What did you notice today that someone else designed without thinking?

directors.name: Michel Gondry
directors.styleDescription: Handmade, surreal, childlike wonder. He films imagination made physical — lo-fi and magical at once.
shootingPrompts: Make something in your environment look impossible
Film an everyday object as if it's magic
Use your hands or body as part of the shot
Create something — fold, stack, arrange — and film it
directors.brief: Make something today that didn't exist before. Even small. Even silly. Film it like it's a magic trick.
directors.question1: Did you make something today, even something tiny?
directors.question2: When did you last feel a small spark of wonder, and what set it off?

directors.name: Bong Joon-ho
directors.styleDescription: Genre-mixing, socially sharp, visually surprising. He films class and absurdity together — always with a twist.
shootingPrompts: Find a contrast in your environment — rich vs worn, old vs new
Film something from an unexpected angle — from below, above
Capture a moment of social awkwardness or tension
Look for irony — something that doesn't quite fit
directors.brief: Find a contrast today that no one else seemed to notice. Capture something from an angle that surprises you.
directors.question1: Did anything today feel slightly absurd in a way that made you smile?
directors.question2: What two things did you see today that didn't belong together?

directors.name: Edgar Wright
directors.styleDescription: Rhythmic, fast, music-driven. He films editing as energy — every cut, every sound, every movement is timed.
shootingPrompts: Film something to the rhythm of a song playing
Use quick cuts — film 5 seconds of 4 different things
Capture a repeated action and speed it up mentally
Find a moment where sound and image land at the same time
directors.brief: Move with rhythm today. Match a beat with what you film. Let sound and image land together.
directors.question1: Did you find your rhythm today?
directors.question2: What was the soundtrack of your day, even if no music was playing?
